thread:
noah: Heads-up — flaky Vitest runs in CI for the JS SDK + sample-app when package.json has "type": "module". Locally green but GH Actions randomly fails with import/mocking errors. Anyone seen this exact combo?
alyssa: Yep. We've hit that. What does the failing trace show?
noah: Example snippets from GH logs: 
```
TypeError: (0 , _inference.createClient) is not a function
 at Object.<anonymous> (src/handler.test.ts:9:18)
```
and sometimes: `ERR_REQUIRE_ESM` in other matrix jobs. TS in runner also yells: "Could not find a declaration file for module '@redwood/inference'".
frank: That screams ESM/CJS interop + test-runner prebundling differences. Are you importing default or named in app code?
noah: App uses default: `import inference from '@redwood/inference'`. Tests use `vi.mock('@redwood/inference', () => ({ createClient: () => ({ predict: () => 'ok' }) }))`.
alyssa: There's the mismatch. Vitest (vite/esbuild) can rewrite modules and your mock replaces the module shape. Two practical short-term fixes: (1) make mocks preserve module shape with `__esModule: true`, or (2) use named imports in tests that match the SDK export shape.
frank: Example shim that preserved shape for me: 
```
vi.mock('@redwood/inference', async () => {
  const actual = await vi.importActual('@redwood/inference')
  return { __esModule: true, ...actual, createClient: () => ({ predict: () => 'ok' }) }
})
```
That prevented the default-vs-named swap. Also set vitest config: `deps: { inline: ['@redwood/inference'] }` so the SDK isn't pre-bundled.
noah: I tried that and it helped locally but CI still flakes on some runs. Any ideas for the TS declarations issue in the runner?
alyssa: Add a test shim `test/types.d.ts` with `declare module '@redwood/inference' { export function createClient(...args:any): any; export default any }` and include it in tsconfig.test.json — quick way to silence tsc in the test env until SDK publishes correct d.ts.
frank: For Jest users you can also get `ERR_REQUIRE_ESM` if jest tries `require()` on an ESM-only package. Long-term SDK fixes: publish dual bundles (dist/index.mjs + dist/index.cjs), include dist/index.d.ts, and add an exports map in package.json with both `import` and `require` entries. That stops most of these flakes.
noah: Did anyone open an SDK issue / repro? I can attach GH actions logs.
ci-bot: Created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/issues/601 (vitest + edge + ESM mock flake) with attached repro and GH actions logs.
alyssa: Also PR suggestion: add a small cjs shim file (index.cjs) that re-exports from the esm build for require consumers, plus add `__esModule` when bundling test dev builds. I opened a draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/620 with exports map + typings tweak.
frank: Good. For sample-app docs we should add a Troubleshooting section in README with recommended vitest config and mock pattern. Quick vitest snippet that worked for me: 
```
// vitest.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config'
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    environment: 'edge-runtime',
    deps: { inline: ['@redwood/inference'] },
    transformMode: { web: [/\.tsx?$/] }
  },
  resolve: { conditions: ['import', 'worker'] }
})
```
And add `test/setup-shims.ts` with the TS shim import so runner picks it up.
noah: I'll add that to the sample-app README and pin a CI matrix that runs node 18/20 + vitest/jest to catch regressions. Keeping issue open until the SDK publish lands. Thanks for the quick troubleshooting! :pray:
